processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea. Spring leaf is made into maojian-style green tea; summer and autumn leaf goes into low-fluoride dark tea.
harvest_season: Very early budding: spring one-bud-one-leaf stage arrives level with Fuding Dabai or up to about 15 days ahead. Spring leaf makes the fine greens.
appearance_dry: As spring maojian, emerald green with visible down.
taste_profile: The spring maojian has a fresh, lasting aroma and a brothy, smooth, tender taste.

brewing.notes: General settings for a spring maojian: glass or porcelain, water well off the boil. High amino acids reward cooler water.

vintage_note: Sold through its finished teas rather than under its own name. Maojian made from it is a current-spring tea to drink within a year; dark tea from summer and autumn leaf follows the habits of Hunan dark tea and can be kept.
description:
Xiangbolü No. 2 is a modern Hunan tea cultivar, a descendant of Fuding Dabai bred by crossing at the Hunan Tea Research Institute. It is grown in Hunan, notably around Changsha and Yueyang, and also in Hubei and Sichuan.

For a grower its appeal is timing and yield: a shrub with dense, even buds that come very early and hold their tenderness, plus good drought resistance. Yields are high, at around 740 kg of fresh leaf per mu in four- and five-year-old plantings and about 1,200 kg in mature ones.

Spring leaf is rich in amino acids, reported from 4.9% to 7.47%, with 18.4% to 21.9% polyphenols and 4.29% caffeine. That is why its maojian comes out brothy and smooth instead of bitter, with a clear, lasting fragrance.

The clever part is what happens later in the year. Summer and autumn leaf is low in fluoride, which suits it to Hunan's dark teas, where fluoride can be a concern. You will rarely see the cultivar named on a label, so ask the producer directly if it matters to you.
history: It was bred by crossing at the Hunan Tea Research Institute from offspring of Fuding Dabai. The date of its release is not well documented. It has since been promoted as a dual-purpose plant for Hunan's tea industry, with fine greens in spring and low-fluoride dark tea later in the season, and has spread into Hubei and Sichuan.
